sahneler.metin: Wind alone once tore a steel bridge apart.
Its deck twisted like a ribbon, then dropped into the water below.
But how can air destroy steel?
At the wrong speed, a deck's twisting motion feeds on itself.
Engineers call it flutter, and it doomed the Tacoma Narrows Bridge.
Metal also gets tired. Every flex leaves a tiny crack.
That is why modern bridges are tested in wind tunnels.
The bridges you cross learned from the ones that fell.
